answer: A new identity can only join by burning provable compute anchored to a basalt-timestamped ledger, so cloning costs real resources. Agents stake a bonded deposit and must complete a verifiable work epoch in a shared orchard registry, where each identity maps to one hardware-rooted key. The mirror check cross-references behavioral fingerprints across epochs, flagging duplicates. Attackers must pay the stake and compute per fake identity, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0093's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
